messages:
kai: heads-up — ap-southeast1 cluster showing a correlated NVMe thermal+read-retry signal; GPU attach latency climbing and a few preemptible hosts already failed attach checks. Anyone on call?

sara: on it. saw the thermal spike around 03:35 UTC, p75->p99 read jumped. Not full device errrors but multiple read-retry bursts on the same physical rack group.

ops-bot: Alert: nvme-thermal-spike (ap-se1) count=12 threshold=5. Incident: INC-20260320-ASE1-NVME.

nate: is this the same cohort we backfilled last week? If so those drives are showing accelerated wear in our telemetry. Could be a batch of drives with hotter thermal profile.

kai: yes, cohort tag: nvme-cohort-batchB. Thermal sensors show ambient +6C vs normal under similar load. Could be datacenter cooling variance + heavy janitor scrubs.

joan: propose immediate mitigations: 1) pause scrub jobs on cohort-batchB for 45m; 2) mark nodes in worst 3 racks as scheduling:degraded so new attachments avoid them; 3) enable local i/o scheduler noop for scratch to reduce cache churn.

ryan: cost/availability trade: marking degraded reduces usable GPU capacity by ~9% in ap-se1. If we divert to other regions, build/test pipelines will see ~30-80ms additional latency. Ops estimate ~4% monthly bill increase if diversion persists 48h.

ops-bot: Command suggestion: `opsctl storage pause-scrub --cohort nvme-cohort-batchB --duration 45m`

sara: running pause now. also toggling runtime prefetch off on serving nodes in the cohort to reduce random reads: `./runtimectl set-flag --prefetch aggressive=false --scope cohort-batchB`

ops-bot: Command executed: pause-scrub (user: sara)  queued.

kai: I've pushed a region-affinity override for ephemeral GPU provisioning to avoid ap-se1 (divert to ap-northeast1 or eu-west2) for non-low-latency queues.

joan: i'll label the three hottest hosts so autoscaler knows to avoid them: `kubectl label node host-ase1-11 degraded=true` etc.

nate: also starting a telemetry dump for the cohort and grabbing SMART exports (`smartctl -a`) from the top 6 noisy hosts. uploading to the incident doc.

ryan: ask HW: can we get firmware rev check? last batch had a firmware that retried reads more aggressively instead of failing to readonly. If we bump firmware to the newer one that flips to readonly on persistent errors maybe safer. But that causes host reboot.

kai: agree test plan: pick a repro host, do a firmware micro-update + scheduler noop flip, observe for 1 hour, then decide rollout. If firmware solves, roll 10% per hour.

joan: reminder: when we mark degraded we should also increase our reserved capacity for latency-critical jobs in other regions to absorb failing attaches. I'll open a slot reservation for 1 hour to avoid immediate throttles.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260320-ASE1-NVME updated: scrub paused; provisioning diversion active; degraded labels applied to host-ase1-11/12/13.

sara: quick note: the thermal telemetry correlates with a maintenance window in the DC 02:00-04:00 local where cooling units were rebalanced. I'll loop infra DC ops. Could be transient.

kai: firmware test scheduled on host-ase1-11 in 12m. owner: nate.

nate: firmware update applied at 04:12 UTC, host rebooted. initial SMART looked noisy but after update read_retries reduced and p99 read latency on that host dropped from 980ms -> 28ms.

ryan: good signal. recommendation: paced firmware rollout across cohort-batchB at 8% hosts/hour, keep scrub paused for 2h, keep diversion in place for 24h, then reassess.

joan: I'll provision temporary capacity in ap-northeast1 for latency-critical builds to avoid failed jobs during the rollout.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260320-ASE1-NVME resolved (provisional). Mitigations: scrub paused, firmware rollout planned, temporary routing rules applied. Follow-up: 24h watch and postmortem.

kai: filing postmortem checklist: root cause hypothesis (cohort firmware + DC cooling rebalance causing thermal hotspots), timeline, mitigations (scrub pause, scheduler noop, firmware rollout, degraded labels, routing diversion), cost impact, and long-term: replace batchB drives on next procurement cycle. Owner: kai.

ryan: thumbs up. keep monitoring. if we see a secondary wave, escalate to #eng-sre.

nate: uploaded SMART dumps and a small script I used to parse read-retry timelines: `scripts/parse_nvme_retries.py --cohort batchB > /tmp/batchb-retries.csv`

joan: thanks team. closing in the channel but keeping incident doc open for 24h.
